question.text: This Spanish king was married to Mary I and sent the Armada to attempt to conquer England.
question.clue: During his reign, an Ottoman fleet commanded by Sufi Ali Pasha was defeated by this king's half-brother John of Austria in the Battle of Lepanto.

swap.leadin: This city-state defeated Athens during the Peloponnesian (PELL-uh-puh-NEEZH-in) War.
swap.text: Name this Greek city-state that was known for its fearless warriors and lunatic attacks.
swap.clue: Every autumn, this city redeclared war on the enslaved helots.

question.text: After the 300 lost at Thermopylae, this Athenian general actually defeated the Persians by organizing a naval defence at Salamis.
question.clue: This man correctly interpreted the prophecy that "wooden walls will defend you and your children."

swap.leadin: Give the following about the aftermath of the 405 BCE Battle of Aegospotami [ay- gus-pah-tuh-mee].
swap.text: At Aegospotami, Lysander led a rout of the Athenian navy, thus essentially ending this war over control of the Greek mainland.
swap.clue: A history of this conflict records emissaries saying "the strong do what they can and the weak suffer what they must" before killing and enslaving the population of Melos.

question.leadin: These people were known as neodamodes when freed.
question.text: Name these ancient slaves of a certain Greek city-state. These people aided the Messenians in the Third Messenian War.
question.clue: Strabo wrote that these people lost their rights during the rule of Agis I, and a group of them was massacred at the Temple of Poseidon in Taenarus.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about bees in Ancient Greece.
swap.text: This culture's Treasury of Atreus is one of their beehive-shaped tombs called a tholos. This mainland Greek culture of the Bronze Age used Linear B script and made the Mask of Agamemnon.
swap.clue: This culture originated the title potnia given to its great mother goddess, constructed huge beehive-shaped tombs called tholoi, and used the Linear B writing system.

question.leadin: While uncovering a "Throne Room" in this city's Palace of Minos, a part time numismatist encountered "lustral basins" that may have been used for purification.
question.text: Name this ancient Minoan city whose 1450 BCE destruction may have been caused by an eruption at Thera.
question.clue: Discoveries near the Dictaean Cave prompted a second attempt to purchase land in Kefala from its Turkish owners; an inability to do so earlier had thwarted the efforts of its original discoverer, Minos Kalokairinos.

swap.leadin: Answer the following questions about the Battle of Leuctra.
swap.text: The Battle of Leuctra unusually saw this fighting force placed on the left side of the army while they were commanded by Epaminondas. This force would later be annihilated by Phillip II at the Battle of Chaeronea.
swap.clue: This group played a major role in winning a decisive victory at the Battle of Leuctra.

question.leadin: Answer the following about items falling on the heads of Ancient Greeks.
question.text: This Greek king was killed after an old woman dropped a roof tile on his head in Argos. This man, the first to use war elephants against Rome, defeated the Romans at Heraclea and Asculum.
question.clue: He launched a campaign with a contingent of war elephants to protect the city of Tarentum, but after victories over the Romans at Asculum and Heraclea, he was forced to retreat from Italy.

swap.text: This German's boyhood dream was fulfilled on the hills of Hissarlik, Turkey, when he found Troy. He also excavated Mycenae, Ithaca, Orchomenus, and Tiryns.
swap.clue: One of this man's most famous discoveries was a golden burial mask belonging to a Mycenaean king, which this archaeologist presumed was Agamemnon.

question.leadin: Answer the following about execution methods throughout history.
question.text: Socrates was condemned to die by drinking the toxic juice of this plant.

swap.leadin: The Mysteries at this site were celebrated until 394AD.
swap.text: Name this city north of Athens which was a celebrated site for the worship of Demeter and Persephone.

question.text: Xenophon's son, Gryllus, died in this battle. Another notable death in this battle was Epaminondas, victor at Leuctra.
question.clue: At a 418 BC battle at this site, Sparta avenged its defeat at Sphacteria by overcoming an Argos-led alliance of democratic states.

swap.text: Following the Battle of Amphipolis, at which both Spartan generals, Cleon and Brasidas, were killed, hostilities were interrupted by this truce, negotiated by its namesake. It lasted less than a year.
swap.clue: It was to be upheld a term of fifty years, though four cities refused to accept it, including Elis.

question.leadin: Emmett Bennett's standardization efforts helped the completion of this task, which was met with initial skepticism until scholars examined the tripod tablet uncovered by Carl Blegen.
question.text: Name this task completed by Michael Ventris, who published a monograph on its results with John Chadwick. Objects found at Tiryns and Pylos helped complete this task.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about the economic history of the successor rump states that emerged from the 1204 Sack of Constantinople.
swap.text: It's not the Morea, but religious silver coins were produced by the mint at Arta that operated under the "Despotate" of this ancient region of western Greece and Albania. Home to the oracle at Dodona, this region's Molossians were led by a king who defeated Rome at Heraclea and Asculum.
swap.clue: That king of this region ignored his advisor Cineas and came to the aid of Tarentum, leading to a defeat at Beneventum.

question.leadin: The 279 B.C.E. Celtic invasion of Greece included a victory at this location, in which Brennus defeated a coalition of Aetolians, Boeotians, Athenians, and Phocians.
question.text: Brennus at first sent warriors swimming across the Spercheios River, but eventually found the same path around this pass that Ephialtes had shown the Persians two centuries earlier.
question.clue: Upon being told to surrender his arms at this location, one military leader issued the famous retort "Molon labe", or "come and take them.

swap.leadin: The engineer Eupalinos blasted a tunnel through Mount Kastro on this island so he could build an aqueduct to supply its capital with water.
swap.text: Name this island ruled in 538 BC by the tyrant Polycrates, who constructed a temple to Hera here dubbed the Heraion.
swap.clue: Herodotus claims that the pharaoh Ahmose broke off Egypt's alliance with this city-state after its tyrant discovered his lost ring in the belly of a fish.

question.leadin: This event was sparked by the execution of Agathocles and opened the door for the Gallic invasion of Greece, as the Macedonian hold on the Balkans became untenable. FTPE.
question.text: Name this 281 BCE battle, sometimes called the last of the wars of the Diadochi, at which Lysimachus was killed by the forces of Seleucus Nicator.

swap.leadin: This event is described in one work with the anecdote of shameless people throwing their corpses onto other people's funeral pyres.
swap.text: Identify this event which killed thousands, including a man who previously gave a notable funeral oration describing his city's support of equality and openness. It is most prominently described in the second book in a series by Thucydides.
swap.clue: Excavations of a mass grave at the Kerameikos in the 1990s prompted analysis of the cause of this event.
